column1: # Can each page_resume row actually ADVANCE its cycle? (2026-10-19)
# WHY THIS SWEEP EXISTS. ENA_PATHOGEN_SARSCOV2_RUNS read 1,000 records of 7,556,500 on every run for ever and
# looked exactly like a healthy no-op: the walk stored no position, which is also what a row that COMPLETES
# inside its ceiling does. It was not that — ebi.ac.uk refuses its second page, so the cycle could never move.
# This asks all 530 cycling rows the same question from data rather than from reasoning.
#   CYCLING       318   a position was stored: the next run reads the next slice
#   COMPLETE      190   the walk ended on its own and cleared it — the genuine no-op
#   STUCK          12   a page FAILED, so no position was stored and the next run re-reads this slice
#   FETCH_FAILED    6   the FIRST page failed; there is no walk to cut short, and the row says so in its own
# THE RESULT, read on the STATUS and not on the verdict: of the 12 STUCK rows, exactly ONE is stuck for a
# reason that is a property of its endpoint, and it is BC_MINERAL_TENURE answering 400 —
#   "Cannot do natural order without a primary key, please add it or specify a manual sort over existing
# GeoServer refuses startIndex on a feature type with no primary key, so that row read 50 of 42,234 for ever.
# Fixed with sortBy=TENURE_NUMBER_ID; measured after, 1,000 records a run over 20 pages, position advancing
# 1000 -> 2000. NOT applied to the tree's 16 other sortBy-less WFS startIndex rows: they were measured too and
# 12 of the 13 reachable ones serve page 2 fine, because GeoServer objects only where the type has no primary
# key. A blanket fix would have been a change made on reasoning.
# The other 11 are 429, 403 and 500 — one reading each, and several are load THIS SWEEP created: 12 jobs in
# parallel, while a 6-job batch-46 emit audit was hitting services6.arcgis.com at the same time (both FAA rows
# are on that host, failing at pages 18 and 20). us-sf-311-open311-requests is already paced at 1200 ms in
# core/hostgate.c and still 429'd at page 20 under that load, which is the clearest sign of the same thing.
# The five au-asic 403s were re-tested BY HAND afterwards and are not reproducible: data.gov.au served 8 rapid
# serial requests and then 12 CONCURRENT ones, all 200. No pacing entry was added on an unreproducible reading.
# A STUCK row is not retired on this: it discloses its own failing page, status and URL in a
# collector-truncation-notice on every run, so re-running this sweep is how a transient is told from a property.
